* This class defines the encoding half of character encoders. * A character encoder is an algorithim for transforming 8 bit binary * data into text (generally 7 bit ASCII or 8 bit ISO-Latin-1 text) * for transmition over text channels such as e-mail and network news. * * The character encoders have been structured around a central theme * that, in general, the encoded text has the form: * * 
 *      [Buffer Prefix]
 *      [Line Prefix][encoded data atoms][Line Suffix]
 *      [Buffer Suffix]
 *
* * In the CharacterEncoder and CharacterDecoder classes, one complete * chunk of data is referred to as a buffer. Encoded buffers * are all text, and decoded buffers (sometimes just referred to as * buffers) are binary octets. * * To create a custom encoder, you must, at a minimum, overide three * abstract methods in this class. *
*
bytesPerAtom which tells the encoder how many bytes to * send to encodeAtom *
encodeAtom which encodes the bytes sent to it as text. *
bytesPerLine which tells the encoder the maximum number of * bytes per line. *
* * Several useful encoders have already been written and are * referenced in the See Also list below. * * @author Chuck McManis * @see CharacterDecoder; * @see UCEncoder * @see UUEncoder * @see BASE64Encoder

methods.name: protected abstract int bytesPerAtom()
methods.comment: Return the number of bytes per atom of encoding

methods.name: protected abstract int bytesPerLine()
methods.comment: Return the number of bytes that can be encoded per line

methods.name: protected void encodeBufferPrefix(OutputStream aStream) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Encode the prefix for the entire buffer. By default is simply
     * opens the PrintStream for use by the other functions.

methods.name: protected void encodeBufferSuffix(OutputStream aStream) throws IOException
methods.comment: * Encode the suffix for the entire buffer.

methods.name: protected void encodeLinePrefix(OutputStream aStream, int aLength) throws IOException
methods.comment: * Encode the prefix that starts every output line.

methods.name: protected void encodeLineSuffix(OutputStream aStream) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Encode the suffix that ends every output line. By default
     * this method just prints a <newline> into the output stream.

methods.name: protected abstract void encodeAtom(OutputStream aStream, byte[] someBytes, int anOffset, int aLength) throws IOException
methods.comment: Encode one "atom" of information into characters.

methods.name: protected int readFully(InputStream in, byte[] buffer) throws java.io.IOException
methods.comment:
* This method works around the bizarre semantics of BufferedInputStream's
     * read method.

methods.name: public void encode(InputStream inStream, OutputStream outStream) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Encode bytes from the input stream, and write them as text characters
     * to the output stream. This method will run until it exhausts the
     * input stream, but does not print the line suffix for a final
     * line that is shorter than bytesPerLine().

methods.name: public void encode(byte[] aBuffer, OutputStream aStream) throws IOException
methods.comment: * Encode the buffer in aBuffer and write the encoded * result to the OutputStream aStream.

methods.name: public String encode(byte[] aBuffer)
methods.comment:
* A 'streamless' version of encode that simply takes a buffer of
     * bytes and returns a string containing the encoded buffer.

methods.name: private byte[] getBytes(ByteBuffer bb)
methods.comment:
* Return a byte array from the remaining bytes in this ByteBuffer. *

* The ByteBuffer's position will be advanced to ByteBuffer's limit. *

* To avoid an extra copy, the implementation will attempt to return the * byte array backing the ByteBuffer. If this is not possible, a * new byte array will be created.

methods.name: public void encode(ByteBuffer aBuffer, OutputStream aStream) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Encode the aBuffer ByteBuffer and write the encoded * result to the OutputStream aStream. *

* The ByteBuffer's position will be advanced to ByteBuffer's limit.

methods.name: public String encode(ByteBuffer aBuffer)
methods.comment:
* A 'streamless' version of encode that simply takes a ByteBuffer * and returns a string containing the encoded buffer. *

* The ByteBuffer's position will be advanced to ByteBuffer's limit.

methods.name: public void encodeBuffer(InputStream inStream, OutputStream outStream) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Encode bytes from the input stream, and write them as text characters
     * to the output stream. This method will run until it exhausts the
     * input stream. It differs from encode in that it will add the
     * line at the end of a final line that is shorter than bytesPerLine().

methods.name: public void encodeBuffer(byte[] aBuffer, OutputStream aStream) throws IOException
methods.comment: * Encode the buffer in aBuffer and write the encoded * result to the OutputStream aStream.

methods.name: public String encodeBuffer(byte[] aBuffer)
methods.comment:
* A 'streamless' version of encode that simply takes a buffer of
     * bytes and returns a string containing the encoded buffer.

methods.comment:

* The ByteBuffer's position will be advanced to ByteBuffer's limit.

methods.comment:
* A 'streamless' version of encode that simply takes a ByteBuffer * and returns a string containing the encoded buffer. *
